rules: Verify Arabic wording against a reliable Quran text.
Do not invent hadith or authenticity grades.
Distinguish classical interpretation from modern interpretation.
Do not describe an interpretation as scientific consensus.
Add exact scientific source titles and URLs only after verification.
Do not classify theological or eschatological statements as experimentally proven science.

research_methodology.standard: Separate the Qur'anic wording, classical tafsir, modern interpretation, and established scientific knowledge.

evidence_grade_meaning.A: Clear, direct match between what the verse describes and what science well understands—still read thoughtfully rather than as a lab textbook.
evidence_grade_meaning.B: Good, helpful connection with observable nature, health, mind, or community life—where context and careful reading matter.
evidence_grade_meaning.C: Open to thoughtful discussion—clear science paired with a broad theme or a verse understood in more than one careful way.
evidence_grade_meaning.D: Faith and spiritual guidance—teaches beliefs, morals, or the afterlife, which belong to faith rather than science experiments.

verification_policy: A scientific source verifies the scientific statement only; it does not verify a theological interpretation.
Classical tafsir must not be silently replaced by a modern scientific reading.
Do not claim the Big Bang is proven by Qur'an 21:30.
Do not claim Qur'an 51:47 unambiguously predicts modern cosmic expansion; classical interpretations include strength, capacity, and vastness.
Do not identify the seven heavens with seven astronomical layers.
Do not turn Last-Day descriptions into experimentally verified astrophysical forecasts.
Arabic text and translation must be checked against a reliable Qur'an edition before publication.
